piece_type: DTC video “An Oprah Special: Shame, Blame, and the Weight Loss Revolution” (ABC primetime 3/18/2024; Hulu) featuring paid consultants and a Lilly executive

cases.claim: [Omission] Boxed-warning contraindication for MEN 2 (only “anybody [who] has a history specifically of medullary thyroid cancer” discussed); W&Ps omitted: severe GI disease, acute kidney injury, hypersensitivity, hypoglycemia, diabetic retinopathy complications, suicidal behavior and ideation
cases.context: Benefit claims by paid consultants (e.g., GLP-1 drugs are “essentially copying what our normal GLP-1 hormone does in our body, but doing it a little bit better”; “double the amount of weight loss”) attributed to Lilly.
cases.rationale: Omits boxed-warning element and multiple W&Ps.
cases.check: Rule: diff risk content vs boxed warning (incl. every contraindicated population) and MG side-effect list; applies to paid consultant/KOL statements.

cases.claim: “There’s been a lot of hype around like pancreatitis, gallbladder complications, concerns for thyroid cancer. This has really not been shown in human studies that this is a downstream complication, and that really the risk is less than 1%.” | “If anybody has a history specifically of MTC... is very, very rare. ... recognizing that it’s rare, but it’s there and we have to always screen.”
cases.context: W&P acute pancreatitis (incl. fatal hemorrhagic/necrotizing); gallbladder disease class W&P; class boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors; 15-yr MTC registry required.
cases.rationale: Minimizes boxed warning and W&Ps by calling them 'hype' and 'rare'.
cases.check: Rule: lexicon flag — 'hype', 'overhyped', 'very rare', 'not been shown' adjacent to boxed-warning or W&P terms.

cases.claim: “I think that they’ve gotten overhyped. Medicines have side effects, but the important part is that they’re mild to moderate in the research studies.” | Dr. Butsch: “Yeah.”
cases.context: Response to patient who discontinued due to nausea and vomiting blood. PI: GI ARs 56% vs 30% placebo (Zepbound); GI-related discontinuations up to 4.3%/6.6%; 'sometimes severe'.
cases.rationale: Characterizes ARs as overhyped and mild-to-moderate when not demonstrated; normalizes risk ('medicines have side effects').
cases.check: Rule: flag 'mild to moderate' / 'all drugs have side effects' framings; verify against PI severity and discontinuation data.

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance / risk prominence
cases.claim: [Format] of a 42-minute video, only about four minutes devoted to shared GLP-1 risks, relegated to the end; no signal where to find more risk information
cases.rationale: Risk not presented with prominence and readability reasonably comparable to benefits.
cases.check: Rule: compute risk vs benefit airtime ratio and placement; flag risk-at-end and absence of risk-source referral.

cases.cat: Failure to submit at first use (Form FDA 2253)
cases.claim: [Process] video not submitted under Form FDA 2253 at initial publication
cases.context: Third-party program; FDA attributed paid consultants' statements to the company.
cases.check: Process rule: inventory paid-consultant/executive media appearances for 2253 submission.
